newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer buys back 110,000 own shares.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer buys back 110,000 own shares.

text.p: Technology corporation Sulzer AG said it and Japanese industrial group Ebara Corp. had decided to discontinue their cross-participation on December 20 and as a result Sulzer has bought back 110,000 of its own registered shares.
The 110,000 shares amount to 4.4 percent of Sulzer's registered share capital, Sulzer said in a statement.
Ebara has also purchased its own convertible notes that were issued to Sulzer for the amount of 66 million francs.
The payments were made by a setoff, Sulzer said.
Sulzer said it had decided not to place the shares in the market but to keep them in treasury stock where they will be reserved for future transactions and the management stock option plan.
The cross-participation between Sulzer and Ebara, a pump manufacturer, concentrated on Japanese and Far Eastern markets and was set up in 1992.
Over the last five years the two parties sought out opportunities for industrial cooperation, but due to changes in business environement no effective cooperation was established.
